The amendment makes `authority.critical_page` differ between rooms at the same tier and channel, but the rollup tie-break (0002:63-69: tier, then channel precedence, then room name) still ignores authority. The rollup then copies `authority` from the winner, and the notifier ladder reads only the rollup. Failure case: Cuisine is `likely`/soft with cooking-attributed heat (`critical_page: false`), and Salon is `likely`/soft with non-cooking heat, which is plausible in the open-plan volume. Both tie on tier and channel, and "Cuisine" sorts before "Salon", so the rollup copies Cuisine's `critical_page: false`. Salon's earned critical page is suppressed. That breaks the amendment's promise that `likely` in Salon is unchanged (0001:330-331). The same collision affects Chambre only when it sorts after the winner. Chambre sorts before Cuisine, so it wins that tie and is safe. The Salon/Chambre test rows (0002:403-404) only cover room verdicts, not the rollup. Remedy: among same-tier rooms, rank `critical_page: true` before channel precedence, or OR critical-page authority across tied rooms. Add a rollup row for Cuisine-cooking `likely` plus Salon `likely`. This changes the aggregation contract, so the rule choice needs author sign-off.

Intent conformance. The intent says "oven plus stovetop heat in Cuisine alone must not raise an iOS critical page" and "Require a second, non-cooking signal ... before critical severity". The amendment adds a restore path with no second signal: "- the heat reaching its +20 K `confirmed` boundary" (0001:323). It also excludes "a heat-earned +20 K `confirmed` in Cuisine that cooking attribution still never erases or downgrades" (0001:329-331, rationale 0001:383-385, test row 0002:402-403). So cooking-attributed Cuisine heat alone at +20 K still pages critically, which contradicts the literal intent. This may be deliberate, since the intent's background says `confirmed` earns a critical page, but the author needs to confirm which rule wins.

`cooking_attribution` is a single value, but the amendment makes two classifications govern the same Cuisine `likely` branch: the heat's attribution and the attribution of a co-present PM2.5 anomaly (see the row 'same heat plus a cooking-attributed PM2.5 anomaly (still `likely`, `critical_page: false`)', 0002:400-401). Nothing says which one fills the field or drives `authority`. Failure case: today no oven or stovetop source exists, so heat attribution is `unknown` (0001:326-328), while #30 can still classify PM2.5 as `attributable` from the Cuisine/Salon gradient. If the field reports the PM2.5 value, the authority rule at 0002:160-162 ('Cuisine `likely` ... with `cooking_attribution: attributable`') sets `critical_page: false`. That silently lowers a page the amendment says must stay critical under unknown heat attribution (0001:319-322), which is a fail-open reading of a missing source. Remedy: state that Cuisine `likely` authority derives from the heat classification only, or expose heat attribution separately. The second option is a schema change and needs author approval.

The round-1 fix (commit 6151442) added the `needs-admission` status in only one of the two places it needs to be. `skills/pr-review-loop/SKILL.md:41-45` now returns `needs-admission` when the Agentic SDLC admission record names no workflow version. It returns `needs-local-review` when the selected-negative-proof binding is missing. The skill's own 'Mutation order' procedure was left behind. Step 2 at `skills/pr-review-loop/REFERENCE.md:209-211` still reads 'Require the delivery owner's accepted local review ... Otherwise return `needs-local-review`', and step 5 at REFERENCE.md:218-220 ('On return, reconstruct authority and require ... accepted local review') does not mention the check either. Failing scenario: an agent follows the step-by-step mutation order for a Workflow 0.2 run whose admission record has no workflow version. It either skips the version check entirely or returns `needs-local-review`, which is exactly the wrong-remedy outcome the round-1 finding set out to remove. Fix: in REFERENCE.md step 2, add that under the Agentic SDLC workflow a missing workflow version returns `needs-admission` and a missing negative-proof binding returns `needs-local-review`, and state which check comes first when both are missing (admission). Then make step 5 point to the same rule.

The round-2 fix does not say which check runs first when the local review and the workflow version are both missing. Step 2 first says 'Require the delivery owner's accepted local review ... Otherwise return `needs-local-review`', and only afterwards says 'Under the Agentic SDLC workflow, first require the workflow version ... else return `needs-admission`'. So 'first' can be read as coming before the negative-proof check only, not before the base local-review check. Scenario: a Workflow 0.2 run has no accepted local review and no workflow version in its admission record. The adapter returns `needs-local-review`, the owner does a full local review, and on return the adapter returns `needs-admission`, which costs an extra round trip. In deliver, admission (step 1) comes before review (step 5), so the admission check should come first. Fix: move the Agentic SDLC sentence ahead of the base local-review requirement in step 2, or say the version check comes before every local-review check. The same ordering applies to SKILL.md:41-45.

That prompt uses the policy to decide ask-user findings under the away posture (bin/fm-branch-prompt.sh:116). The same prompt's role limits forbid the branch to 'post publicly, or send anything outside this home's fleet' (bin/fm-branch-prompt.sh:101) and say these limits 'hold in every posture' (bin/fm-branch-prompt.sh:103). Concrete path: the captain is /afk, the branch declines a simplification finding as an author call, and the repository has a writable tracker. The skill then points the branch at a gh issue it may not create. The branch either breaks its role limit or skips the step, and the note is lost at cleanup again, which is the failure this change is meant to close. Fix: add one sentence saying that a decision made under the away posture (the supervision branch) always uses the held backlog-item home and never files a project issue. The backlog wrappers are not actor-guarded, so the branch can use them.

The backlog home is two steps: `bin/fm-tasks-axi.sh add`, then `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold`. But `fm-captain-hold.sh hold <id> --title ... --reason ... [--origin <task>]` already creates a missing row and holds it in one guarded step. It also creates the row with `--kind captain` and records `--origin` provenance, which ties the note back to the ticket that is being cleaned up. The captain-hold-lifecycle skill (lines 20-22) names that path. Narrower form: use the single `hold --title ... --origin <task-id>` call instead of add plus hold.

The round-1 fix (f2) introduced this problem. It moved the whole author note into `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold ... --reason <note>`. The previous two-step form could carry the note in the `tasks-axi add` body instead. `hold` rejects a reason that is more than one line (bin/fm-captain-hold.sh:830 validate_one_line) or contains parentheses (bin/fm-captain-hold.sh:831, tasks-axi hold contract). Line 53 requires the note to state the finding, the reason it was declined, and the suggested change so that it stands alone. Notes like that routinely span lines or contain parentheses, for example `fn(x)`, file:line references, or "(e.g. ...)". Concrete path: firstmate declines a simplification finding and runs the prescribed command with a multi-line note. `hold` fails before it creates the row, so the durable home is not written until the agent notices and rewrites the note. The note may also get trimmed until it no longer stands alone. Fix: state in the skill that the `--reason` note must be a single line with no parentheses.

Rule 8 tells the worker to put the full inventory (one entry per comment: reviewer, file, line, claim — see header at bin/fm-brief.sh:109-113) in its "first status note". In the same brief, rule 4 (bin/fm-brief.sh:640-646) says a status note is a single appended `{state} [at=<epoch>]: {one short line}` line (STATUS_APPEND, bin/fm-brief.sh:350) that wakes firstmate and should be sparse. Take a continued PR with 8 Codex comments: the worker has to either cram 8 structured entries into one status line or append several lines. Extra lines have no state prefix, or each one wakes firstmate. Either way the status protocol that firstmate's watcher and the fleet ledger consume gets broken or overloaded. The intent only asks that each comment be listed with whether the pipeline covered it; it doesn't say the list goes in the status file. Where the list should go instead (the worker's terminal/report, the PR body, or a single status line pointing to a file) is a product decision, so this needs the author's call.

The proxy host forwards to `http://192.168.42.33:8096`, but the Jellyfin settings (operations.md:35-41) never set Known Proxies or LAN networks. Traffic from NPM reaches the bridge-networked container from the Docker gateway or the NPM address. If Known Proxies is empty, Jellyfin ignores X-Forwarded-For and treats every internet client as local network. The per-user 'allow remote connections' control and remote bitrate limits then have no effect, and activity and auth logs record the proxy IP instead of the real client. Jellyfin's reverse-proxy docs require Known Proxies for this reason. This is unverified against the host; `GET /System/Configuration/network` (KnownProxies, LocalNetworkSubnets) would settle it. consume_authorization never rechecks health or the lane's control state, and InRunAuthority.allow only compares `now` with the health expiry fixed at issue time. At t0+5m the next Curator cycle fails, for example with an ERROR outcome or a failed keep write. run_cycle sets last_failed_cycle_id and disarms the lane (cycle.py:301-305), so evaluate_health now reports the lane unhealthy. Sibling site: InRunAuthority.allow (authorization.py:269-283) should end the authority when the state shows a failed cycle newer than token.cycle_id or the lane is disarmed.

Introduced by fix round 1 (the F1 fix). _standing_problems treats a replaced heartbeat the same way as a failed cycle or a disarm. A routine, successful scheduled Curator cycle therefore pauses the lane or raises a critical alert. Sequence: a token is issued at t0, the lane's next scheduled cycle succeeds at t0+5m and rewrites the heartbeat (lane still ARMED, no newer last_failed_cycle_id), and the runner consumes at t0+6m. consume_authorization raises AuthorizationRefused(global_pause=True), so a runner that honours global_pause pauses the lane after a normal overlap. Refusing or ending on a new heartbeat is the right direction, because the new cycle may have re-judged members. The fix is to split the classification: return a plain refusal for a heartbeat replaced by a newer successful cycle (non-critical end in-run; the caller reissues against the new cycle), and keep global_pause and critical only for disarm, a fault, a changed armed bundle, a newer last_failed_cycle_id, or an unauthentic heartbeat. Sites: authorization.py:280-289 (classification), :336-338 (in-run critical end), :392-394 (global_pause on consume).

`--request-budget` is compared only with the candidate count. The pre-flight `/models` request and up to `max_retries` extra 429/503 requests per call also count as requests (`requests_sent` counts them). A budget equal to the candidate count can therefore still run out mid-cycle, and for an approved A the resulting ERROR disarms the lane. The README says the budget is the operator's own count, so this note is only informational.

Simplification: `RETRYABLE_STATUSES` retries HTTP 503 as well as 429. The intent requires only 'pacing and retry of HTTP 429 inside one call'. The narrower form, retrying only 429, meets the intent. Keep 503 only if the author wants provider-overload retries as well.

Simplification: the new `model_requests` block in the curator-run JSON output and the `requests_sent` / `throttled` counters on the client are not required by the intent. They are operator telemetry. Suggested remedy: remove them unless the author wants this output.

If the shadow B fails pre-flight, the whole cycle is skipped, including the approved A. `_preflight` puts A and B in one list of problems (cli.py:306-322), and any entry for B skips the run and returns 3 (cli.py:350-356). Inside a cycle, a B ERROR never disarms anything: only A's ERROR judgments become faults (cycle.py:213-217). The skip also writes no heartbeat, and health expires at min(T+2I, H+24h) (health.py:226), after which the watchdog disarms the lane. Concrete case: A is Mistral and B is Gemini with `--b-request-budget 20` (the suspected ~20/day free limit), and a bundle has 25 candidates. Every approved cycle is then skipped with 'B: the cycle needs 25 requests but the budget is 20'. A never judges, its heartbeat goes stale, and the lane disarms. The same happens whenever Gemini's model list returns 429 or 401. So the shadow variant's quota controls the live lane, which is the outcome the intent's pre-flight is meant to prevent. This still fails toward protection, but it disarms the lane for a shadow-only reason. Suggested remedy: when only B fails pre-flight, drop B (run with proposed=None and report B as skipped) and skip the cycle only for A's problems. This changes when A runs without a comparison, so the author should decide.

The fix in e3b1165 (`allow_abbrev=False`) stops `--api-key sk-...` from being read as `--api-key-env`, but the key still leaks. `mrctl curator-run ... --api-key sk-secret-XYZ` exits 2 with `mrctl: error: unrecognized arguments: --api-key sk-secret-XYZ` on stderr, and the same happens for `--b-api-key` and `--api-key-e`. The secret therefore still reaches any captured log (cron, User Scripts), which is the leak the round-1 finding described. The commit title says 'so API keys never echo', but the new test `test_an_abbreviated_key_flag_is_refused_without_echoing_its_value` checks only that the old 'sk-secret is not set' message is gone. It never checks that the value itself is absent, so it passes while the key is still printed. Suggested fix: in `main`, call `parser.parse_known_args(argv)`; if there are leftover arguments, call `parser.error` naming only the leftovers that start with `-`, never their values. Then make the test assert that `sk-secret` appears nowhere in stdout or stderr. See s9-abbreviated-api-key-refused.transcript.txt.

You can't pipe a value into `bws secret create` as the guide says. The local `bws secret create --help` shows `Usage: bws secret create [OPTIONS] <KEY> <VALUE> <PROJECT_ID>`, and the command has no stdin option. So 'piped from the host into `bws secret create`, never printed' in rotation step 1 (line 40), and 'host → Mac stdin → `bws secret create`' in Phase 1 (line 75), can only be done by putting the value into argv on the Mac, for example `"$(cat)"`. That breaks ADR 0012:48, which says values never appear 'in command arguments', and the credential policy. Rotation step 2 (line 42) has the same problem: 'Create the new value' on an existing `<name>` needs `bws secret edit --value`, which also takes the value in argv. Fix: document a path the CLI supports, and state openly that the value is briefly in argv on the Mac. Alternatively, move writes to the web vault or the SDK, and narrow the ADR rule to host-side argv.

Phase 8 generates a goldwin deploy key and then removes the old `authorized_keys` line after only checking 'from a fresh shell' and repointing `unraid-ssh`. None of its steps updates the goldwin runner's GitHub repository secret to the new deploy key or tests a goldwin deploy before the old line is removed. The secret stays on the old key because of D3 and the injection row at line 57. An operator following Phase 8 as written would break goldwin deploys the moment the old line is deleted. Fix: add 'update the goldwin repository secret and verify a deploy' as a stop condition before 'remove the old line'.

Phase 7 tells the operator to 'delete `/boot/config/credentials/`', but its rollback says 'restore from quarantine and the dated `go` backup'. No step moves the credentials to quarantine, and no step takes the `go` backup. Phase 7 also never creates the array-start user script that the injection table (line 55) says must copy `/mnt/user/appdata/secrets/host/` into place. Following the phase as written, the operator deletes the boot credentials without the replacement mechanism or a rollback copy in place. Fix: list the steps in order: back up `go`, install and test the user script, quarantine `/boot/config/credentials/` (not delete), then revoke the old tokens. Phase 3 (line 78) has the same gap: its rollback relies on a 'dated template backup' that none of its steps takes.

Phase 9 says to 'Sign Unraid Connect in again' and 're-enable its flash backup', but no earlier phase signs out of Unraid Connect or disables its flash backup. D8 says to 're-enable its flash backup after rotation', which implies it is off during Phases 3 to 8. As written, no step routes the operator to that disable action, so the flash backup could keep uploading old secrets while they are being rotated. The doc also never states or cites whether it is off on the host today. Fix: add a disable/sign-out step before Phase 3 (or in Phase 2), or mark the current state as unverified and name the check that settles it.

The `Write a key` pattern added in fix round 1 reads the value with `IFS= read -r value`, which keeps only the first line. ADR 0012:8 puts the root SSH private keys in Secrets Manager. Phase 1 (line 94) says to capture every current value 'as in Write a key', and Phase 8 (line 101) says to store the new keys the same way. For an OpenSSH private key, `value` becomes just `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`. `bws secret create` then succeeds and stores a truncated, unusable key with no error, and Phase 8 later removes the old key on the strength of that stored copy. Fix: tell the operator to use `value=$(cat)` for multi-line values (trailing newlines are stripped), or send multi-line values (PEM or OpenSSH keys) through the web vault. The same one-line read appears at `line 30` (`read -r value` on the host in `Read a key`), and a consumer of a multi-line key would hit the same truncation there.

Fix round 1 added 'Take a dated backup of `/boot/config/go`' to Phase 7, and the rollback restores that backup, but no step says what to change in `go`. No file in the repository shows that, and the doc does not mark it unverified. After Phase 7 moves `/boot/config/credentials/` to quarantine, the copy lines in `go` would still run at every boot against files that are gone. The flash would also keep a stale mechanism, and the operator has a backup of a file they were never told to edit. Then add the step 'remove those lines from `go` and check it with `sh -n /boot/config/go`' (as tooling/infra/log-fill-fix.md:112-113 does) before the quarantine move.

The last commit removed `--allowedTools Read,WebSearch` along with the isolation flags, so web search may no longer be allowed. `claude_args` now passes no permission grant at all. In Claude Code, reading files in the working folder needs no approval, but WebSearch does. In `claude -p` a tool that needs approval is denied automatically unless the user's own settings already allow it. On the Unraid server, a fresh container with only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` has no such settings. Each check would then fail to search, and the prompt at claude.py:67-70 tells Claude to leave `comparisons` empty when search finds nothing. The report still shows a price section with no comparisons, and no error is raised. On the Mac the result depends on whatever `~/.claude/settings.json` happens to allow. This conflicts with the intent's "Claude reads the listing text and the photos and can search the web". The fake claude always reports `webSearchRequests: 3`, so the tests cannot catch this. Suggested fix: pass `--allowedTools WebSearch`. That grants access rather than restricting it, but it changes the permission settings, and the owner asked for Claude Code's "normal permission settings", so they should decide. Also check that the Mac live run actually produced price comparisons with links.

The model check requires `set(response['modelUsage']) == {self.model}`. In print mode, Claude Code's `modelUsage` usually lists every model the CLI used during the session, not only the one that wrote the answer. That often includes a small helper model (a `claude-haiku-*` entry) used for internal background calls. The key can also be the resolved full model id instead of the exact string passed to `--model`. Unverified: no live `claude-code` run has been made, as the README says. It can be settled with one `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... claude --print --model claude-opus-5 --output-format json --json-schema '{...}' <<< 'hi'` run on the host, then reading the `modelUsage` keys. If a helper model does appear, every judgment becomes an ERROR. That fails toward protection, so it is safe, but it makes the default backend useless. The tests lock in this strict reading: the 'extra-model' scenario in tests/test_curator_claude_code_client.py treats an extra haiku entry as an error. The intent requires 'an error when the answer ... comes from a different model', and it does not settle whether an auxiliary model that did not write the answer counts as a different model. Options: (a) keep the strict check; (b) require the pinned model to be present and allow only known auxiliary entries; (c) test the live output first. This is a product decision about the judgment contract, so the user should choose.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve trailing newlines in multiline secrets**

Contrary to this statement, Bash command substitution removes every trailing newline from `$(cat)`. That deterministically changes multiline values such as the SSH private keys this guide explicitly handles; for example, removing the final newline from an OpenSSH Ed25519 private key makes `ssh-keygen -y` reject it with `error in libcrypto`. The current `jq -r` recipe happens to append one newline when reading, but the vault no longer contains the valid value and retrieval through the web UI, SDK, or a non-`jq -r` path can produce an unusable key. Capture the bytes with a sentinel or another newline-preserving method.

Live model probe and live-run status.

Probe on 2026-09-29, Claude Code 2.1.284, on a Mac's own Claude login with no Curator data: `claude --print --model claude-opus-5 --output-format json --no-session-persistence --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"word":{"type":"string"}},"required":["word"],"additionalProperties":false}'` returned `structured_output` `{"word":"ok"}` and `modelUsage` keys exactly `["claude-opus-5"]`, the same string passed to `--model` (not a resolved full id). The model check therefore matches the `--model` string exactly, requires it in `modelUsage`, and allows only `claude-haiku-*` helper entries beside it, which each judgment records as `helper_models`.

The live Curator run with a `claude setup-token` subscription token has not been made: it waits for the token to be created and stored in Bitwarden Secrets Manager (project Unraid). The pipeline's test step drove 2 of 8 scenarios live (missing token; real CLI with an invalid token and a stray ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, which returned an OAuth 401 as an ERROR with no API-key fallback and no token in output). The helper-model, wrong-model, invalid-output, and usage-limit cases are covered by the fake-`claude` tests in `tests/test_curator_claude_code_client.py`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear alternate-provider variables before launching Claude Code**

When `curator-run` inherits an environment configured for another Claude Code provider, `_environment()` preserves routing switches and credentials such as `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, AWS credentials, or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; the [Claude Code Bedrock configuration](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/amazon-bedrock) explicitly uses such environment variables. Consequently, this supposedly subscription-only backend can attempt a billed cloud/API call despite removing the two Anthropic key variables. Use an allowlisted environment or explicitly remove all alternate-provider and endpoint variables. The live host environment was not checked; `env | rg '^(CLAUDE_CODE_USE_|ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL|AWS_|GOOGLE_)'` would establish whether it is currently affected.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop retrying every candidate after a CLI timeout**

If the Claude CLI hangs during an outage, this exception becomes one candidate's `ERROR`, but `_judge_all` continues and starts the CLI again for every remaining candidate because only usage-limit failures are latched. With the documented roughly 90-title cycle and the 600-second default timeout, one outage can keep a cycle running for about 15 hours—longer than the PRD's maximum 12-hour expected interval—before recording the failed cycle. Treat a timeout or equivalent process-wide failure as sticky for the remainder of the cycle, as the usage-limit path already does.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate subscription-wide failures to both lanes**

When the approved Claude variant reaches the shared subscription usage limit, this generic `ModelError` is converted by `_judge_all` into candidate `ERROR` judgments, and `cycle.py` then records every `ERROR_OUTCOME` with `shared=False`. The failure path therefore disarms only the lane currently running, even though `PRD.md:318` requires both lanes to be disarmed for shared authentication or model faults; the other lane can remain ARMED against its previous healthy heartbeat and still receive an authorization until it runs or expires. Preserve a shared-fault classification for subscription-limit and authentication failures so the cycle disarms both lanes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the Claude Code binary version in variant identity**

The recorded variant identity contains only the runtime label and requested model, so replacing or auto-updating the `claude` executable leaves `model_version` unchanged. Claude Code itself supplies the system/runtime behavior around structured output, tools, helper calls, and authentication, so two different CLI releases can produce different judgments while passing version-drift checks and consecutive A/B comparison gates as the same approved variant. Pin the executable version or include the verified `claude --version` value in the variant identity so an upgrade requires review and promotion.
